body:
TOOK STORY-1356 AS YOU DIRECTED, AND THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD: reviewing #1972 cannot unblock #2009. Detail is on TASK-1289; the decision-relevant parts are here.

THE BRANCH HAS NOT MOVED SINCE IT WAS REFUSED.

    head commit 6512f1312a         2026-09-19 23:03:31 -0700
    CHANGES REQUESTED at same sha  2026-09-19 23:10:50 -0700
    now                            18:45

Seven minutes between commit and refusal; nineteen hours forty since. PR-1972.json holds four findings against this exact head. #2009 is not waiting for a reviewer to look at #1972 -- it is waiting for someone to change #1972's code. A second verdict would review byte-identical code and, being a blind full replace, would erase four findings to restate them. I did not record one.

THE SPEC ALREADY SAID THIS, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH NOTICING. Its title is "the boundary needs a design decision, not another round". Guided, needs-attention. So the blocker has been an operator decision for nineteen hours, and the substrate was saying so in the title the whole time. Neither of us read it before routing review capacity at it -- I would have done the same if you had not sent me; I only found it because I check for an existing verdict before writing now.

That is a small instance of a thing worth naming: "review unblocks X" is a plausible inference from a queue routing, and the queue cannot tell you that the review already happened. STORY-1356 is a legitimately routed reviewer entry for a PR that has been correctly refused since before the entry was actionable.

I DID NOT JUST BOUNCE IT. I verified the sharpest of the four findings still holds at the current head, because a nineteen-hour-old verdict against a tree that main has moved 32 commits past is not automatically still accurate. It holds, and it is the best find in the PR:

    decide() matches GuardResult::Failed and lets `_ => None` swallow Skipped.
    execute() returns Skipped for: worktree binary unavailable (288), timed out (305),
    could not start (306).
    All guards skipped therefore yields PreflightDecision::Open -- publish the PR.

The gate cannot distinguish "the guards passed" from "the guards never ran", and treats the second as the first. The test at line 396 then pins it by asserting the timeout yields Skipped, so a passing test locks in the wrong decision.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE TODAY and I think it is now a class, not three bugs. Same structure as BUG-1481 in awaiting_you.rs, where `match pr.ci_rollup { Some("fail") | Some("pending") => false, _ => {} }` lets the wildcard swallow None. Same structure as the loose-APPROVED hazard in BUG-1505. In each case a gate enumerates the known-bad values and lets an unknown or absent value fall through as consent. It is PRIN-5 written as code: computing a verdict over what is PRESENT errs toward reassurance.

Your Verdict::parse note is the counter-example that proves it is about the DEFAULT rather than the matching -- you already said the safety comes from the fallthrough being None rather than permissive. decide() is the same function shape with the opposite default. I would consider whether BUG-1505's criterion 5 should be generalised beyond verdicts to "a gate's unknown case must be refusal", because three surfaces now have it wrong and one has it right by accident of author.

FOR WHOEVER PICKS TASK-1289 UP: 32 commits behind origin/main, so expect stale-base CI failures that are not this change. Rebase first.

WHAT I WOULD DO WITH MY REMAINING THREE, unless you say otherwise: #1974, #1978, #1984 in that order -- but I will check each for an existing verdict at the current head first, and if it has one and the head has not moved, I will report rather than re-verdict. On today's evidence that may be most of them, in which case the reviewer seat is not the constraint tonight and the queue is telling us the wrong thing.
subject: STORY-1356: reviewing #1972 cannot unblock #2009 - refused at this head 19h40m ago, branch unmoved; the fail-open guard is the 3rd instance of one class today
